subject: Post-call econ sizing: streaming vs batch mixes + next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Walker <tom.walker@novacare.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call econ sizing: streaming vs batch mixes + next steps

Hi Tom / Elena —

Great to meet earlier — quick recap and a couple items we need to size a clean ballpark for you. Thanks for the context on workflows. I tried to capture the important splits below so we can run unit economics and propose a short PoC scope.

Recap of flows (from our call)
- Interactive agent (user chat in the app): ~60% of requests, median prompt+reply token length ~320 tokens, peak QPS expected ~30 regionally, target p50 latency ~150ms, p95 <350ms.
- Background enrichment (async): ~40% of requests, longer contexts (avg 1,200 tokens), can accept higher latency (1–3s).
- Authentication/compliance: data needs to remain in US region; SOC2 evidence will be shared by Marissa.

Asks to finalize a ballpark estimate
1) Can you confirm an approximate monthly token volume (total input+output)? If you prefer a range, send low/expected/high.
2) Target budget range (monthly) or target $/1M tokens you want to hit. This helps us choose hosted tier vs dedicated and whether to suggest low-latency streaming nodes or batching/quantized variants.
3) Any hard SLOs (p95 latency, or max cold-start) beyond what we discussed for interactive flows?

Early guidance / what we'll run for you once we have numbers
- For interactive-heavy workloads with p50~150ms we usually recommend a low-latency streaming configuration (smaller batch windows, prewarmed kernels). That typically trades up to ~2–3x unit cost vs cost-optimized batching on quantized models.
- For mixed workloads a multipath policy (streaming for interactive; batch-quantized for async enrichment) often reduces total bill by ~30–45% vs streaming-only while maintaining UX.

Next steps
- Please attach the token profile spreadsheet (Ive attached a blank template) and drop your low/expected/high numbers.
- If budget looks like it aligns, we propose a technical deep-dive next week (infra + ML runtime) — Marissa and Grace will run the sizing + MAP.

Attaching: novacare_token_profile.xlsx (fill and return).

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Tom Walker <tom.walker@novacare.ai>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call econ sizing: streaming vs batch mixes + next steps

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the template. Quick answers below while we fill the sheet:

Estimated monthly volume (rough):
- Low: 12M tokens / mo
- Expected: 35M tokens / mo
- High: 80M tokens / mo (if feature scales regionally)

Workload split (approx):
- Interactive agent: 60% of API calls, ~65% of tokens
- Async enrichment: 40% calls, heavier token per call but fewer calls

Budget & target unit economics
- Our procurement/finance team is looking for an operating target near $700 / 1M tokens (as a blended target). We understand there will be variance by config.
- Monthly budget range for initial pilot: $8k - $18k (we can commit more for production).

SLOs
- Interactive: aiming for p50 <200ms, p95 <400ms — user-facing so latency matters.
- Async: p95 acceptable up to 3s

Compliance
- Please include SOC 2 type II evidence in the package (procurement asked). I've attached our procurement checklist.

We'll fill the spreadsheet and send it back by Monday. If you can provide a quick ballpark for blended bill at 35M tokens with a 60/40 split (interactive/async) that would help internal alignment before the deep-dive.

Tom Walker
Head of Product, NovaCare
tom.walker@novacare.ai
Attached: novacare_procurement_checklist.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Walker <tom.walker@novacare.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call econ sizing: streaming vs batch mixes + next steps

Tom / Elena —

Thanks for the numbers — helpful. I ran a quick back-of-envelope for a 35M token month with a 60/40 interactive/async split and included two realistic configuration options so you have trade-offs up front. These are illustrative; we'll refine after we get the filled sheet.

Assumptions used
- Interactive avg 320 tokens/transaction (prompt+response), Async avg 1,200 tokens/transaction.
- Interactive requires streaming nodes to hit p50~150–200ms; async can be served on cost-optimized quantized variants with batching.

Option A — Low-latency (streaming-first)
- Config: hosted low-latency streaming tier (prewarmed, 2x concurrency per GPU), standard model (non-quantized) for best response quality.
- Estimated blended unit cost: ~$1,050 / 1M tokens.
- 35M tokens -> ~$36,750 / month (pilot; excludes volume discounts).
- Pros: meets p95 <400ms comfortably, simplest integration.
- Cons: higher unit cost vs batching.

Option B — Multipath (streaming + batch-quantized) — recommended starting point
- Config: streaming for interactive (smaller fleet), cost-optimized quantized model pool for async with 2–3s batching windows and autoscaling. Smart routing policy to send each request to the right path.
- Estimated blended unit cost: ~$620 / 1M tokens (weighted by the 60/40 split).
- 35M tokens -> ~$21,700 / month (pilot; excludes committed-discount).
- Pros: ~40% cheaper vs streaming-only while keeping interactive latency targets.

Discounting & committed volume
- With a 12-month committed capacity at expected volumes we typically can discuss tiered discounts that bring Option B toward your $700 / 1M target (especially after quantization and multi-hour batching windows on async).

Next steps I propose
1) Marissa/Grace to run a technical deep-dive (runtime + infra) to validate SLOs and sizing; aim for Thursday 30 Jun (US morning).
2) You return the filled token_profile spreadsheet; procurement attach SOC2 we have a standard evidence pack we will share.
3) If you prefer, we'll scope a 4-week pilot: measure token billing, latency SLOs, and a readout.

Attaching an initial MAP draft so procurement & engineering have a starting plan: redwood_map_draft.pdf

If that looks reasonable I'll lock the Thurs slot and Marissa will send the calendar invite.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Karthik / team —

Thanks, that is very helpful and gives us something concrete to show finance. Thurs 30 Jun morning works for the technical deep-dive — please send a 60-min invite.

Two quick clarifications before the call so we can prepare finance:
1) Can you give a very quick ballpark for monthly spend at 35M tokens (60/40 split) after a modest committed discount (we're thinking a 10–15% commit discount for a small pilot)? Your Option B number of ~$21.7k pre-discount — with a 12% commit discount that would be ~ $19k — does that sound right?
2) For the multipath config: anything we should be concerned about in terms of implementation complexity or runtime maintenance (e.g., model parity issues between quantized async model and full-fidelity streaming model)?

Procurement will bring SOC2 questions to the call.

Elena Ruiz
Dir. Platform Engineering, NovaCare
